In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surat al-Nasr

Medinan, and its verses are three.

It is the last surah to be revealed, according to a report from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father.

Al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn Abbas that when this surah was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, my death has been announced to me."

[p-6285]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[1-3] ﴿When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest,﴾ ﴿and you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes,﴾ [An-Nasr: 2] ﴿So exalt your Lord with praise and seek His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.﴾ [An-Nasr: 3]

﴿When the victory of Allah has come﴾, i.e., the victory of His true religion over falsehood. "And the conquest", i.e., the conquest of Makkah, which Allah opened between him and his people, may the blessings of Allah be upon him. He granted him dominance over them and weakened their resolve to cling to their false beliefs.

﴿And you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes﴾ [An-Nasr: 2], i.e., you see people from the various kinds and tribes of the Arabs, at that time, entering into the religion of Allah, which is your religion that you brought to them, once the veil that stood between them and it has been removed, which is the veil of the strength of falsehood. So they will turn to it in multitudes, in groups and communities, not individually, as was the case at the beginning of the matter during the days of hardship. All of that came about, and it is without doubt bound to occur.

﴿So exalt your Lord﴾ [An-Nasr: 3], i.e., declare your Lord free from neglecting the truth and leaving it to falsehood to devour it, and from failing to fulfil His promise of supporting it. This declaration of His freedom from such things should be accompanied by praising Him and extolling Him as the One who is Mighty, whom no overpowering one can overcome, and the Wise, who, when He grants the disbelievers respite in order to test the hearts of the believers, will never waste the reward of those who do good, nor set right the deeds of the corrupters. And the All-Seeing of what is in the hearts of the sincere and the hypocrites, so the showing-off of the corrupters is not hidden from Him, and the All-Seeing of what is in the hearts of the sincere and the hypocrites, so the display of the ostentatious is not hidden from Him.

﴿And seek His forgiveness﴾ [An-Nasr: 3], i.e., ask Him to forgive you and your companions for whatever anxiety, impatience and sorrow there was, due to the delay in the time of victory and conquest. Seeking forgiveness (istighfar) comes only through sincere repentance. Repentance from anxiety comes only through perfecting one's trust in the promise of Allah and making this trust prevail over the thoughts of the soul that hardships produce. Although this is something difficult for human souls, Allah knew that the soul of His Prophet (ﷺ) could reach that perfection; [p-6286] therefore He commanded him to do it. Likewise, the hearts of the perfected among his companions and followers, peace be upon him, come close to it. And Allah accepts from them.

﴿Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾ [An-Nasr: 3], i.e., He, glorified is He, is always described as one who greatly accepts repentance, because He is a Lord who trains souls through trials. When it finds weakness, He raises it to seek strength, and strengthens its resolve through the goodness of His promise, and He continues with it until it reaches perfection. At every station it repents from the one before it, and He, glorified is He, accepts its repentance; so He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful. It is as if Allah were saying: When the conquest has come, the victory is realised, and the people turn to the true religion, then fear has been lifted and the cause of sorrow has passed away. Nothing remains but glorifying Allah, thanking Him, and turning to Him away from whatever thoughts had arisen in the soul. The hardship will not return to seize the souls of the sincere as long as they remain in that abundance of sincerity. From this the Prophet (ﷺ) understood that the matter had been completed and nothing remained for him except to journey to his Lord. So he said, as is reported from him: "Indeed, his soul has been announced to him." This is the summary of what the Imam included in his tafsir.

Notes:

First: Ibn Kathir said: The meaning of "the conquest" here is definitely the conquest of Makkah. For the tribes of the Arabs were waiting in suspense regarding their acceptance of Islam until the conquest of Makkah, saying: "If he prevails over his people, then he is a prophet." So when Allah granted him the conquest of Makkah, they entered into the religion of Allah in multitudes. Within two years the Arabian Peninsula was thoroughly unified in faith, and there remained among all the tribes of the Arabs none but those who outwardly professed Islam, and to Allah belongs praise and grace. Al-Bukhari related in his (Sahih): "From Amr ibn Salamah: We were at a water-place on the route of the people, and riders would pass by us, and we would ask them: 'What is the matter with the people? What is the matter with the people? Who is this man?' They would reply: 'He claims that Allah has sent him and has revealed to him,' or 'Allah has revealed such-and-such.' I used to memorise those words, and it was as if they were being impressed upon my chest. The Arabs were waiting to accept Islam until the conquest, saying: 'Leave him and his people, for if he prevails over them, then he is a true prophet.' So when the event of the conquest of Makkah occurred, every people hastened to accept Islam, and my father hastened on behalf of my people in accepting it..." The hadith.

Second: Al-Razi said: If we take "the conquest" to mean the conquest of Makkah, then there are two views regarding the time of the revelation of this surah:

One of them: The conquest of Makkah was in the eighth year (AH), and this surah was revealed in the tenth year. It has been related that he (ﷺ) "lived seventy days after the revelation of this surah"; for this reason it was named the Surah of Farewell.

The second: This surah was revealed before the conquest of Makkah, and it is a promise to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that He would support him against the people of Makkah and grant him the conquest of it. A parallel to this is: ﴿Indeed, He who has ordained the Qur'an for you will surely bring you back to a return﴾ [Al-Qasas: 85]. And His saying: ﴿When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest﴾ requires the future tense, since one does not say of what has already happened "when it has come" or "when it occurs". If this is valid, then this verse is among the miracles, since it is a report whose content was found, after some time, to correspond to it; and reporting the unseen is a miracle. End of quote.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in (Fath al-Bari): Abu Ya'la related, from the hadith of Ibn Umar: "This surah was revealed in the middle of the days of Tashriq, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) knew that it was the announcement of his farewell."

Then he said: I was asked about the statement of al-Kashshaf that the Surah of Victory was revealed during the Farewell Pilgrimage in the days of Tashriq; how then can it begin with (idha), which indicates the future? I answered that what he transmitted is weak. And even if it were sound, the condition was not completed by the conquest, because the coming of the people in multitudes had not yet been completed, so the remainder of the condition is still in the future tense.

Al-Tibi raised the objection and answered it with two answers:

One of them: (idha) may come in the sense of (idh), as in His saying: ﴿And when they see a trade﴾ [Al-Jumu'ah: 11], and so on.

The second: the speech of Allah is eternal. Both answers are open to considerable scrutiny. End of his words.

Third: Al-Shihab said: The word "the people" here means the Arabs, so the definite article is one of prior reference (ahd). Or it means the customary totality, and what is meant is the idol-worshippers among them, because the Christians of Taghlib did not accept Islam during his lifetime, and they paid the jizyah.

Fourth: Al-Bukhari related from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) did not pray after this was revealed to him: ﴿When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest﴾, without saying in it: 'Glory be to You, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me.'"

Also in it, from her: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say much in his bowing and prostration: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me,' interpreting the Qur'an."

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: The meaning of "interpreting the Qur'an" is that he applied what he was commanded regarding glorification, praise and seeking forgiveness to the most noble times and states.

Ibn al-Qayyim said in (al-Huda): It is as if he took this from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and seek His forgiveness﴾ [An-Nasr: 3]: "For he used to make seeking forgiveness the conclusion of matters; so when he finished the prayer he would say: 'I seek the forgiveness of Allah' three times." And "when he came out of the lavatory he would say: 'Ghufranaka' (Your forgiveness)." And the command to seek forgiveness at the conclusion of the rites of pilgrimage has come: ﴿Then depart from where the people depart, and seek the forgiveness of Allah﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 199], and so on.
